opened.title: fix(port): the threads reading a track are stopped before the program exits
opened.author: ReaperOfVeriod
opened.untrustedBody:
## What

A music track is read and decoded on a thread of its own, and the thread was
detached: nothing waited for it. The player can close the window while a track
is being read, and the program then exits (`std::exit`) with that thread still
running. The static destructors take the mutex and the stream list away under
it, and the thread locks a mutex that no longer exists: a crash at quit, which
the crash handler catches and writes a report for. The launcher then says the
game stopped unexpectedly, when the player only closed it.

The readers are kept now, and the program stops them and waits for them before
it exits: in `leave()` (the window closed, the game ended) and through an
`atexit` handler for the other ways out (a run of so many frames, an error).
A reader that is already decoding finishes first, so nothing is taken away
under it.

## Why it is not the sound output's thread

The sound output's own thread was already stopped before the program's globals
go (`56413059`, an `at

opened.author: ReaperOfVeriod
opened.untrustedBody:
A bug sweep of the launcher: 32 fixes, each in its own commit. Nothing here
changes what the launcher does on purpose; every commit fixes something it did
by accident.

## The ones that could lose data, or start the wrong thing

- **A backup name could reach outside the memory card.** The name of a backup
  to restore was joined to the card's folder as it came: an absolute path
  replaced the card's folder, and `..` climbed out of it. The restore removes
  the card's own folders first and then copies the backup's into their place,
  so a name from outside the card replaced the player's saves with another
  folder's contents. Only a name that is one folder of the card's own

merged.author: bigmak94

## What

The game assembler gives every `mfc1` the MIPS I coprocessor-load delay, so it puts a `nop` between an `mfc1` and an instruction that reads its target. Retail never has that `nop` in compiled code, so no function containing the pair could match from C.

+               && ! cop_interlocks

merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## What this pull request changes

This is the review of #239 applied. Three findings, each addressed.

The game assembler gives every `mfc1` the MIPS I coprocessor-load delay, so it puts a `nop` between an `mfc1` and an instruction that reads its target. Retail never has that `nop` in compiled code, so no function containing the pair could match from C.

opened.author: bigmak94
opened.untrustedBody:
## What

The levels' rotated id-list walks (entry tests, the body, then the test chain again at the bottom: `lh -2(p)` with `bgezl`, `beql p, table[g]`) come out of this cc1 with a dead `lh $v0,-0x2(...)` at each walk's entry. Retail has none: no level function of the 7,765 keeps such a load. Any C for these walks was a few words short of retail, and 39 catalogue functions have this entry.

**Cause.** The jump pass before cse2 copies the walk's test in front of the loop. cse2 folds the copy's `p == table[g]` test but leaves its jump, which now leads only to the next block. This EE tree comes from the March 1999 trunk. There, flow's `delete_unreachable_blocks` tidies an edge into the next block only if the edge is not marked fallthru, and a conditional jump to the next block has its two edges merged into one fallthru edge. opened.title: fix(levels): tighten the filler rule and drop the epilogue residues
opened.author: llesieur99
opened.untrustedBody:
## What this pull request changes

This is the review of #239 applied. Three findings, each addressed.

**The padding rule was too loose.** It accepted every `addu`, not just a move of
`$zero`, and every `addiu` whose *destination* was `$sp`, not one that adjusts
`$sp` by `$sp`. So `addu $t0,$t1,$t2` (arithmetic) and `addiu $sp,$a0,16` (a
write through a register) passed for filler. The operands now matter.

**A four-byte row that follows a body's epilogue is not filler.** `func_0029CB50`
is a four-byte row holding `addu $v0,$v1,$v0`, and the previous body ends with
`jr $ra` and its delay slot: the word is what that body left behind. It is not
the linker's padding - the words say otherwise - so it is measured by its own
rule, `is_epilogue_residue`, and dropped from the catalogue.

merged.title: Make the build and try tools run natively on Windows
merged.author: chistianh
merged.untrustedBody:
The README says Windows works natively with Git Bash (`bash tools/build.sh`), but on a plain Windows install every compile failed:

1. `cc.sh`, `build_libgcc.sh`, `build_libm.sh`, `compile_variants.sh` and `try_variants.py` always call `wine`, which does not exist on Windows (the 32-bit compilers run directly there).
2. `try_func.py` writes `Path.relative_to()` into `compile.sh`, which gives backslashes on Windows; bash reads them as escapes, so the compile never runs (it reported `COMPILE failed` for every candidate, and left stray `buildtry…log` files in the repo root).
3. `try_func.py` / `try_variants.py` fall back to `tools/docker/run.sh` when `wine` is missing, which on Windows is not needed (and usually not installed).
